GO applies to the audit, not publication or a winner declaration.","findings_by_draft":{"D01":{"factual_support":"Supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046; the distinction between accepted access and authorized action is explicitly bounded inference.","usefulness":"The instruction to inspect ‘one sensitive action’ gives leaders a manageable review task.","distinctness":"The opening and key metaphor change presentation, but the reasoning and inspection task recur in D02, D09, D10, D13, D14 and D15.","naturalness":"‘The front door accepted the key’ is accessible; ‘That is a question to test, not a prevention claim’ adds an unnecessary second disclaimer.","needed_edits":["Remove the closing disclaimer after retaining the paragraph explaining the limits of the comparison.","Replace ‘final enforcement point’ with ‘where the payout executes’ for a less abstract leadership prompt."]},"D02":{"factual_support":"The incident descriptions are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. ‘It is reasonable for leaders to take confidence’ is editorial framing, not a sourced finding about leaders.","usefulness":"Clear inspection task, but it takes several paragraphs to reach it.","distinctness":"A conciliatory opening changes tone rather than the underlying telling; its argument and action closely match D09 and D13.","naturalness":"‘The question is what that confidence establishes’ is measured, but ‘For leaders, that distinction deserves explicit examination’ is generic.","needed_edits":["Open with the concrete authorization distinction and remove the unsupported generalization about leaders’ confidence.","Delete ‘For leaders, that distinction deserves explicit examination’ and move directly to the inspection task."]},"D03":{"factual_support":"The dummy-reference mechanism is supported by CIAD-2026-0046; Cloudflare containment is supported by CF2024. ‘Consider a thought experiment, not a performed test’ correctly distinguishes an invented illustration from evidence.","usefulness":"The paired requests make the approval question inspectable and explicitly acknowledge limits concerning binding, replay and coverage.","distinctness":"Genuinely distinct diagnostic telling: it moves from an observed mechanism to a controlled hypothetical comparison and interpretation of results.","naturalness":"‘Failed baselines or inconsistent outcomes’ and ‘on that modeled path’ read like test documentation rather than a short leadership post.","needed_edits":["Qualify ‘Both proceeding would expose a missing approval requirement’ to cover an absent or ineffective enforcement rule: if the policy requires a matching approved record, both proceeding would show that the modeled path does not enforce it.","Replace ‘Failed baselines’ with ‘If the approved request also fails’.","Shorten the Cloudflare comparison if the payout thought experiment remains the central argument."]},"D04":{"factual_support":"The reported incidents and named bypassed checks are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. The narrow inference is appropriately identified.","usefulness":"‘Can a request ... reach execution without that check?’ directly targets a consequential architectural question.","distinctness":"More explicit about containment and bypassed checks than the basic comparison drafts, but still substantially the same access-versus-authorization telling.","naturalness":"The opening is economical. ‘An access signal can remain accepted after legitimate control of its use has been lost’ is much less readable.","needed_edits":["Replace the abstract ‘access signal’ sentence with ‘A stolen credential can still be accepted; that does not authorize the action requested.’","Reduce repetition between ‘Valid access. Unauthorized action.’ and ‘The credentials worked.’","If retaining ‘with no customer data or global network changes affected,’ use ‘Cloudflare reports no affected customer data and no changes to its global network.’"]},"D05":{"factual_support":"The incident mechanism and recommendations are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. ‘My reading’ and ‘Imagine a hypothetical payout’ clearly identify inference and illustration.","usefulness":"Connects approved records to transaction-stage binding while correctly warning that a matching record alone is insufficient.","distinctness":"The hypothetical missing-record request and explicit record-sufficiency caveat provide a substantive difference from the generic inspection drafts.","naturalness":"‘What did acceptance prove?’ is direct. ‘These separate supplied accounts’ sounds like an evaluation artifact rather than Graham’s published voice.","needed_edits":["Change ‘one service token and three accounts stolen’ to ‘credentials for one service token and three accounts’ to avoid implying that accounts themselves were stolen.","Use ‘approved record’ instead of ‘sanctioned record’ for a general business audience.","Replace ‘These separate supplied accounts were not independently verified here’ with a concise attribution-based limitation appropriate to publication."]},"D06":{"factual_support":"The October mechanism and November recurrence and non-production-to-production movement are supported by CIAD-2026-0046 and CIAD-2026-0058. Ownership assignments and operating decisions are labeled proposals; the held request is labeled hypothetical.","usefulness":"The strongest operational handoff: business owners define payment requirements and technical owners demonstrate enforcement. It also separates local operating decisions from advisory evidence.","distinctness":"Genuinely distinct governance telling, combining payment authorization, remediation evidence and responsibility for deciding which paths may operate.","naturalness":"‘The payment references led nowhere’ is vivid. ‘Local authorization, enforcement and remediation evidence’ and ‘operating decision’ are dense abstractions.","needed_edits":["Add 2026 to ‘October 9’ and ‘November 4’ for standalone clarity.","Keep ‘Under this proposed policy’ because holding for review is the author’s policy illustration; CIAD-2026-0046 specifically recommends rejecting references without records.","Replace ‘evidence of investigation and completed remediation’ with a concrete request for forensic verification of eradication, attributed to CIAD-2026-0058.","Trim the final paragraph if the business-and-technical-owner handoff has already been stated."]},"D07":{"factual_support":"The payment mechanism, renewed attacks, incomplete remediation and forensic-verification guidance are supported by CIAD-2026-0046 and CIAD-2026-0058. ‘A completed remediation checklist’ is not a reported feature of the incidents.","usefulness":"Combines approved-payment evidence with evidence of recovery, but introduces two substantial leadership decisions in a short post.","distinctness":"Genuinely distinct extension from transaction approval to recovery assurance, though it overlaps D06’s remediation theme.","naturalness":"‘The same demand for evidence applies to recovery’ is a smooth transition. The closing ‘The reason to trust it may not’ leaves the referent and recovery implication vague.","needed_edits":["Replace ‘It does make a completed remediation checklist an insufficient basis for restoring trust’ with ‘My recommendation: require forensic evidence of eradication before relying on a remediation checklist.’ This preserves the inference without implying the advisory documented completed checklists.","Identify the November advisory as an update in the same reporting chain.","Replace the ambiguous closing with a concrete request for approval and eradication evidence."]},"D08":{"factual_support":"The credential history, containment, bypassed checks, mule transfers and approved-record recommendation are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. ‘The comparison concerns a trust assumption, not equivalent damage’ accurately bounds the comparison.","usefulness":"Turns the conceptual distinction into a specific approved-transaction question and attributes the corresponding recommendation.","distinctness":"Its explicit unequal-outcomes comparison and source-backed approved-record action go beyond synonyms, although the core structure remains close to D15.","naturalness":"The opening is crisp but ‘Invalid conclusions’ is broad. ‘A consequential mechanism’ is unnecessary editorial scaffolding.","needed_edits":["Change ‘one service token and three accounts stolen’ to ‘credentials for one service token and three accounts’.","Replace ‘with a consequential mechanism’ with the mechanism itself.","Keep the approved-record question and recommendation; condense the incident-outcomes paragraph if brevity is needed."]},"D09":{"factual_support":"Both incident summaries are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046; the access-versus-action distinction is bounded inference.","usefulness":"The final inspection instruction is concrete, but most preceding interpretation repeats the first sentence.","distinctness":"Not a materially new telling relative to D02 and D13: it adds explanatory restatements to the same evidence and action.","naturalness":"‘The credentials were accepted. That did not make the attackers’ access legitimate’ is clear; repeating the distinction after each incident slows it down.","needed_edits":["Remove ‘The distinction matters for business and IT leaders’ and its restatement.","Retain only one short interpretation after the incident evidence."]},"D10":{"factual_support":"The incident facts and distinction between first-party and sector reporting are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046.","usefulness":"Offers the standard inspection task with strong evidence boundaries.","distinctness":"Primarily a hook-and-caveat variation on D01, D09 and D14, not a new argument or action.","naturalness":"‘The inspection question is concrete: Inspect’ repeats itself, while the long caveat paragraph interrupts momentum.","needed_edits":["Delete ‘For business and IT leaders, the inspection question is concrete’ and proceed directly to the task.","Condense the caveat while preserving the different-source and no-effectiveness-claim boundaries.","Remove ‘The supplied accounts have not been independently verified here’ from post copy unless that process disclosure is intended for readers."]},"D11":{"factual_support":"CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046 support the incident summaries. The office-door illustration is explicitly an analogy, not a reported incident.","usefulness":"The key/invoice distinction can help a nontechnical reader understand the argument.","distinctness":"A genuine explanatory device, but the remainder is the same evidence, conclusion and inspection task as the controls; it is not a separate substantive route.","naturalness":"‘A working key gets you through the office door. It does not approve an invoice’ is accessible. Immediately explaining the analogy’s limits makes it feel overmanaged.","needed_edits":["Shorten the analogy qualification to ‘As an analogy’ or integrate that signal into the opening.","Remove the next thesis paragraph if the analogy already establishes the distinction."]},"D12":{"factual_support":"CIAD-2026-0046 supports missing records and payout validation; CF2024 supports reported containment. ‘Compromised entry need not erase downstream boundaries’ is bounded inference, not a universal effectiveness finding.","usefulness":"Separates two useful questions: what authorizes execution, and what limits damage after compromise.","distinctness":"Genuinely distinct two-part telling. Cloudflare supplies a containment dimension rather than merely another example of stolen credentials.","naturalness":"The opening is concrete, but the final paragraph compresses trust, scope, records and segmentation into a dense set of abstractions.","needed_edits":["Replace ‘previously trusted access becomes insufficient evidence when its connection to current authorization, purpose or scope is uncertain’ with a direct statement that accepted access alone does not prove transaction approval.","Separate the two closing questions into short sentences with their respective actions.","Describe Cloudflare’s reported outcome as ‘no affected customer data and no changes to its global network’ rather than ‘no customer data or global network changes affected.’"]},"D13":{"factual_support":"The factual summaries are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. The conclusion remains a conceptual inference.","usefulness":"The inspection question is actionable but carries almost all the practical value.","distinctness":"Mostly synonymous restatement of D09 and D02: ‘entitled to carry out’ substitutes for ‘permission’ without changing the reasoning.","naturalness":"‘An access check answers only part of the question’ is clear, but the draft explains that same point three times.","needed_edits":["Delete the paragraph beginning ‘The distinction matters’.","Keep one thesis sentence, the evidence, the inspection task and a short limitation."]},"D14":{"factual_support":"The incidents are supported by CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. ‘Not a matched comparison’ accurately identifies an evidence limitation.","usefulness":"Retains the standard inspection task but adds no new inspection method.","distinctness":"Mostly D10 with an extra rhythmic sentence and another comparison caveat; these are presentation changes.","naturalness":"‘The credentials passed’ is readable, but ‘The business purpose still needed scrutiny’ weakens the more precise requirement for authorization.","needed_edits":["Remove ‘The business purpose still needed scrutiny’ or replace it with ‘That did not establish authorization for the transfer.’","Merge the two comparison-limit paragraphs.","Delete ‘the practical question is specific’ before the question itself."]},"D15":{"factual_support":"The incident paragraphs directly cite CF2024 and CIAD-2026-0046. ‘My reading’ cleanly marks inference, and the comparison caveat avoids unsupported prevention claims.","usefulness":"A focused, manageable instruction: inspect the payout where it executes and ask what enforces approvals despite accepted access.","distinctness":"A polished version of the core comparison route, not a fundamentally different argument from D01 or D10. Explicit source markers and the integrated execution question improve editorial usability.","naturalness":"The most cohesive general-leadership version of that route. ‘Accepted access signals have limits as evidence of legitimate action’ is its most abstract sentence.","needed_edits":["Replace the abstract ‘accepted access signals’ sentence with ‘A working credential does not prove that a payout was approved.’","Make the final question name an approved underlying transaction, while retaining the broader requirement for approvals and business checks.","For publication, resolve the source markers to the supplied source links."]}},"comparison":{"human_preference":"Pending; no human preference or measured audience response is available.","overall_support":"All drafts have support for their central reported mechanisms. The main issues are inference wording, compressed credential terminology and repetition, rather than invented incidents.","distinct_tellings":[{"labels":["D01","D02","D04","D08","D09","D10","D13","D14","D15"],"assessment":"One broad cross-incident access-versus-authorization family. D08 adds an explicit approved-record recommendation; D04 emphasizes execution and containment. Most other differences are hook, rhythm, caveat placement or synonyms."},{"labels":["D03","D05"],"assessment":"Hypothetical payment illustrations provide a different explanatory method. D03 offers a paired diagnostic comparison; D05 illustrates an enforcement rule and warns that record existence is insufficient."},{"labels":["D06","D07"],"assessment":"A distinct payment-and-recovery family. D06 emphasizes owners and operating decisions; D07 emphasizes forensic evidence after remediation."},{"labels":["D11"],"assessment":"A distinct analogy, attached to the standard argument and action."},{"labels":["D12"],"assessment":"A distinct authorization-and-containment structure, supported by different contributions from the two sources."}],"editorial_tradeoffs":"D15 is the clearest general-leadership starting point with direct attribution and limited scope. D06 offers the richest operational handoff but needs more room and covers recovery as well as payment approval. D03 is strongest for a diagnostic discussion but is more technical. D12 supplies a second substantive control question at the cost of focus.","selection_basis":"Editorial judgment based on factual discipline, usefulness, coherence and required revision; not a winner declaration or a prediction of human preference."},"strongest_single_draft_label":"D15","proposed_hybrid":{"base_label":"D15","contributing_labels":["D08","D05"],"steps":[{"action":"Retain D15’s attributed incident comparison and bounded inference.","evidence":"D15 says ‘My reading’ and ‘They do not establish that a particular defense caused different outcomes’; these keep interpretation separate from reported facts."},{"action":"Make D15’s final inspection question concrete using D08’s approved-record requirement: ask what verifies an approved underlying transaction and enforces the required checks when the direct API call executes. Attribute the record-validation recommendation to CIAD-2026-0046.","evidence":"D08 asks whether ‘a payout instruction is supported by an approved underlying transaction’ and names the recommendation to reject references without corresponding records."},{"action":"Add a short sufficiency qualification without importing a second hypothetical: ‘A matching record alone does not prove that every authorization check was completed.’","evidence":"D05 explicitly states ‘A matching record alone would still not prove every authorization check was completed.’ CIAD-2026-0046 separately recommends stage binding, maker-checker approval and beneficiary validation."}],"complementary_strength":"D15 supplies the coherent attributed structure, D08 supplies a specific inspection object, and D05 prevents that object from being mistaken for complete authorization. This is a targeted revision, not an accumulation of all routes."}},"claim_support":[{"source_id":"CF2024","reported_facts":"Credentials from the October 2023 Okta compromise were mistakenly considered unused and left unrotated; attackers later accessed Cloudflare’s Atlassian environment. Cloudflare reports that segmentation and other controls limited lateral movement, with no affected customer data and no global network changes.","evidence_location":"Opening and October18 timeline; Opening containment summary.","boundary":"First-party retrospective from a different organization, period and system; it does not demonstrate payout-approval controls or comparative control effectiveness."},{"source_id":"CIAD-2026-0046","reported_facts":"Attackers invoked fund-transfer APIs with stolen credentials from victims’ whitelisted infrastructure, bypassed application checks, supplied dummy references without corresponding records and transferred funds to mule accounts.","evidence_location":"Description; Key TTPs Observed.","boundary":"Reported campaign observations, not evidence about the reader’s own system."},{"source_id":"CIAD-2026-0046","source_recommendations":"Validate payouts against approved records; reject references without corresponding records; cryptographically bind transaction stages; require maker-checker verification and other payment checks.","evidence_location":"Recommended Actions.","boundary":"Recommendations, not measured prevention rates or proof that matching records alone establish authorization."},{"source_id":"CIAD-2026-0058","reported_facts":"Successful attacks continued against entities that had undertaken remediation, including deliberate re-targeting after incomplete remediation. Non-production environments provided entry paths to production through shared credentials, tokens or network paths.","evidence_location":"Overview; Description.","boundary":"An update in the same CERT-In reporting chain, not independent corroboration or proof that fully implemented controls failed."},{"source_id":"CIAD-2026-0058","source_recommendations":"Perform full eradication with forensic verification and continue periodic threat hunting after incidents.","evidence_location":"Recommended Actions.","boundary":"Does not establish that a completed checklist was documented in the reported incidents or determine when a particular organization can safely resume payouts."},{"type":"editorial_inference","statement":"Accepted credentials or network origin alone do not establish business authorization.","supporting_source_ids":["CF2024","CIAD-2026-0046"],"boundary":"Conceptual interpretation of the supplied reports, not a matched causal comparison."},{"type":"hypothetical_illustration","draft_labels":["D03","D05","D06"],"statement":"Synthetic or imagined payout requests illustrate questions about approval enforcement.","boundary":"No test was performed; proposed outcomes depend on the stated policy and modeled path."}],"limitations":["Assessment uses only the supplied source text and claim summaries; no external verification was performed.","Cloudflare’s supplied evidence includes summarized claims rather than a complete article reproduction.","Human preference is pending. Naturalness, usefulness and editorial selection are judgments, not measured audience outcomes.","The CERT-In advisories are one reporting chain; Cloudflare is independent but not a matched comparison.","No editing-time measurements or editing-effort estimates are asserted.","No draft was posted, and publication has not been requested."]}
